surviving_claim: In the tested single-writer process-SIGKILL model, v0.25 future-row deletion and fixed-tail truncation are restart-convergent at the exercised cleanup boundaries. Interrupted cleanup preserves the exact committed logical snapshot; repeated restart converges to zero hidden future rows and zero stale file-length tail with zero application logical redo; abandoned future rows do not resurrect after a later epoch advance.
non_claims: a file-length truncate observed after process SIGKILL before explicit fsync is not a hardware power-loss durability guarantee
SQLite internal WAL-frame and fsync behavior is not measured
filesystem allocated-block reclamation and storage-device cleanup work are not measured
multi-writer recovery, distributed consistency, production latency, throughput, and cost are not established
